Everyone says India is becoming a convenience economy.
I think we're actually becoming a habit economy.

Look at this list.

Rapido: 8.2 crore monthly active users
Blinkit: 7.9 crore
Swiggy: 6.7 crore
Zomato: 6.3 crore
Uber: 3.9 crore
Ola: 2.7 crore

None of these companies manufacture what they sell.

They don't grow vegetables.
They don't cook food.
They don't own most of the bikes or cars that move people

Yet millions of Indians open these apps every single day.

That's because they aren't competing to deliver groceries or rides anymore.

They're competing to become the first app your thumb reaches for.

The biggest shift in consumer tech isn't faster delivery.

It's reducing the number of decisions people have to make.

Hungry? Open Swiggy or Zomato.
Need groceries? Blinkit.
Need to reach somewhere? Rapido or Uber

The less we think, the more these apps win.

That's why the real metric isn't downloads.

It's how often people come back without even realizing it.

The strongest consumer brands aren't just solving problems.

They're quietly becoming part of our daily routine.

And once a product becomes a habit, competitors don't just have to build a better app.

They have to break an existing behavior.

That's one of the hardest things in business.

The next billion-dollar company may not be the one with the newest idea.
It could simply be the one that earns a permanent place in our everyday habits.
